notes:
The page continues the classification by proper subgroups H of Z, then bears the underlined heading “Orientation d'un contour”. It gives two conditions labeled “Conditions équiv.”, defines the orientation set, asserts two inverse orientations in the strict case, and states the automorphism action, index-two kernel, cyclicity and a half-direct-product corollary. The initial strict is both inserted and canceled; the later strictness qualification is attached to the cardinality assertion. The small inverse sentence is an interlinear insertion before Alors. Two contour sketches, the abandoned three-line c) definition and its unfinished “[i.e.” are retained. The duplicate g in the rewritten a) sentence and final “une orientation fixé” remain as written. The later Aut superscript is unresolved (e/epsilon/c/+); the algebra does not select its ink.

Mathematical checks: under distinct vertex/edge adjacency, the four-cycle refutes the asserted equivalence (M006-E). Label vertices modulo 4: g(s)=1−s sends every vertex to a neighbor, but fixes two edges and exchanges two disjoint edges; g(s)=−s gives the reverse failure. Complete enumeration of all eight automorphisms confirms that requiring both conditions selects only the two unit rotations (M006-O4). For a connected strict contour, the separately checked conjunction refinement M006-O gives the two unit rotations, cyclic translation kernel and semidirect product by inversion. This does not validate the written equivalence, which is transcribed unchanged. The two-vertex/two-parallel-edge case has automorphism group C2×C2 and, under the conjunction, a singleton orientation set (M006-D2); thus the later two-element target/index assertion needs strictness if that case was intended to be included. These checks prompted attention to Conditions équiv., the canceled strict, the c=card S≠2 insertion and Aut superscript; each was decided from its crop. Reader checks M006-K and M006-I establish only the conditional kernel-index inference and elementary inverse-pair cardinality.

No secure explicit authorial doubt formula or date appears. The canceled heading abbreviation is not expanded into an authorial claim. Archive foliation 5 is retained only as a comment; there is no author page count.

events.who: GPT-6 Astra Pro; effort inherited/not exposed; scan006 main preliminary check
events.outcome: Refined conditional statement: for a nonempty connected strict contour, define an orientation by the conjunction of both written distinct-adjacency conditions. Then there are exactly two orientations, inverse to one another; conjugation on them is onto C2, its kernel is the cyclic translation group, and Aut(X) is the corresponding semidirect product by inversion. Proof using M005-C: label vertices of a finite cycle by Z/n (n>=3), or of the infinite path by Z, with edges {i,i+1}. An automorphism is determined by two adjacent images and unique continuation, hence is i -> b + epsilon*i, epsilon=+1 or -1. A translation satisfies the vertex condition exactly for b=+1 or -1, and these also satisfy the edge condition. A reflection has a fixed vertex when n is odd, or when b is even for even n or the infinite path; otherwise it fixes an edge. It therefore fails at least one distinct-adjacency condition. Conjugation by a reflection interchanges the two unit rotations, while all translations fix them. Thus the action is onto C2 and its kernel is exactly the translations. This checks a strengthened/conjunction interpretation, not the manuscript claim that either single condition suffices.
